quote: Amendment No. 1 § 2.1 replaces § 11.2 so that the exclusions are now: (a) Supplier's indemnity obligations under § 9.1, "which are excluded solely to third-party intellectual property claims under Section 9.1(c)"... 1. Recall costs are now capped. The original § 11.2(b) (uncapped recall costs) is deleted with no replacement... 2. Most of Supplier's indemnity is now capped. Only IP infringement claims (§ 9.1(c)) remain uncapped. Supplier's indemnity for product defects (§ 9.1(a)), personal injury or death (§ 9.1(b))... are all subject to the six-month-fees cap.
reason: The memo states that Amendment No. 1 replaces Supply Agreement § 11.2. It notes that recall costs are no longer carved out of the cap and that the indemnity carve-out now covers only third-party IP claims. It also explains that product-defect, personal-injury and recall exposure is now limited to the six-month-fees cap. That matches the criterion in substance. One small discrepancy: the memo cites Amendment § 2.1 where the ledger says Section 2, which is consistent.
